exact_semantics_role: L2 exactness is not independently refuted. A sound all-fields linear-algebraic observer may remain partial/OPEN on properties outside its expressiveness; the theorem blocks universal L1 totality under preserved L2 soundness.

fixed_global_transition_model.name: FIXED_POINT_PLUS_ALL_FINITE_FIELD_LINEAR_ALGEBRAIC_OPERATORS
fixed_global_transition_model.semantics: The implicit global decision/progress language extends fixed-point logic by linear-algebraic operators acting on vector spaces over finite fields of all prime characteristics. This is broader than original FPR and includes the all-primes finite-field direction needed to remove the fixed-prime defect.

published_theorem.title: Limitations of the invertible-map equivalences
published_theorem.statement_used: Combining CFI constructions over fields and over the rings Z_{2^i}, the authors prove that no fixed k makes invertible-map equivalence using the set of all primes coincide with isomorphism on all finite graphs. They conclude that no extension of fixed-point logic by linear-algebraic operators over fields can capture polynomial time.
published_theorem.witness_type: Polynomial-time decidable isomorphism/CFI properties outside the all-finite-field linear-algebraic logic.

derived_TRUMP_barrier.claim: Even with all finite-field linear-algebraic operators, the fixed implicit language cannot discharge universal L1 while preserving L2 exactness on all relevant finite structures.
reason: R44AG's FPC model misses fixed-field affine solvability; R44AH's original FPR misses uniform prime-parametrized rank.
The all-primes theorem goes beyond both defects: even linear-algebraic operators over every finite-field characteristic leave PTIME properties outside the language.
A sound mechanism may respond OPEN on those properties, preserving L2, but then it does not satisfy L1 universal totality.
The separating constructions use ring-valued CFI structure over Z_{2^i}, identifying algebraic information not reducible to vector spaces over fields.

dead_zone_mapping.meaning: The correct outcome outside the language is OPEN, not a false terminal verdict.

what_is_not_proved: L2 exact semantics is not refuted for partial outputs.
No barrier is claimed for fixed-point languages equipped with sufficiently general finite-ring/module operators unless separately proved.
No Turing-machine runtime lower bound is claimed for finite-field or finite-ring algorithms.

TRUMP_architecture_consequence.rule: Do not identify global algebraic state with finite-field rank/matrix state. A universal implicit invariant must state exactly which algebraic domains/operators it supports and remain soundly OPEN outside proven scope.

next_admissible_math.question: Does a precisely fixed finite-ring/module extension overcome this field-only expressiveness barrier, and what is its proved boundary?
